claim_scope: fixed episode-reward weights move a two-phase scalar action target toward the successful subset mean
the same weighting reduces effective sample size and the normalized weight assigned to recovery examples
a per-phase marginal range gate accepts an unseen action combination that a nearest-complete-trajectory gate rejects
all-success and all-failure groups have zero unnormalized leave-one-out advantage while a mixed group retains relative signal
rejecting zero-advantage groups changes the used context distribution and requires separate attempted, rejected, and used denominators

code.config: standard-library v3 reward-reweighting and dynamic-rejection fixture

limitations: four scalar trajectories and a hand-authored successful-subset reference
episode-level binary labels rather than learned rewards, per-step credit, advantages, or human corrections
weighted action means rather than an optimizer or policy update
no VLA, world model, simulator, LIBERO, checkpoint, GPU, robot, or vehicle
joint-support gate uses a hand-authored nearest-trajectory MAE threshold and is not a density, reachability, or safety estimator
leave-one-out fixture omits normalization, policy ratios, clipping, KL penalties, repeated resampling cost, and optimizer dynamics
dynamic-rejection difficulty labels and outcome groups are hand-authored and do not estimate RIPT-VLA task prevalence or performance
